methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specifications were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, functionalities, and constraints. Each statement was broken down to its most granular, self-contained meaning. The goal was to create independent units that could be individually assessed for coverage and similarity. Truth table entries, module declarations, signal descriptions, and logical operations were all treated as potential atomic units.
mindtraced_atomic_units: JK flip-flop behavior is defined by a truth table.
The module has inputs clk, j, and k.
The module has an output Q.
When J=0 and K=0, Q(t+1) = Q(t).
Q(t+1) represents the next state after the clock edge.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, j, and k, and output Q.
Q_next is the next value of Q based on j, k, and Q_old.
The combinational logic can be implemented using AND, OR, and NOT gates.
j, k, and Qold are input signals.
AND gates generate product terms: (!j & !k & Qold), (j & !k), and (j & k & !Qold).
An OR gate combines the product terms to produce Q_next.
The output Q changes its value only on the positive edge of the clock signal clk.
The next value of Q depends on the current values of j, k, and the current value of Q (previous state).
The next state of Q depends on the setup time of j and k relative to the positive edge of clk, and the clock-to-output delay from the positive edge of clk to when Q becomes valid.
The module contains one register, Q, which is declared as output reg Q.
The value of Q is updated using a non-blocking assignment (<=) within an always @(posedge clk) block.
When j=0 and k=0, Q retains its previous value.
When j=0 and k=1, Q becomes 0.
When j=1 and k=0, Q becomes 1.
When j=1 and k=1, Q toggles its value.
